title: Multimodal datasets: misogyny, pornography, and malignant stereotypes

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative and quantitative auditing of the LAION-400M dataset and CLIP-retrieval system using gendered search terms (e.g., 'school girl', 'CEO', 'housewife') to identify hyper-sexualization, NSFW content, and occupational stereotyping, alongside testing CLIP's cosine similarity filtering on misogynistic image captions.

Querying the dataset with racial, ethnic, and nationality terms (e.g., 'Asian', 'Black-woman', 'Latina', 'Desi', 'African', 'European') to evaluate visual fetishization, the prevalence of NSFW-flagged metadata, and analyzing CLIP's susceptibility to racist and conspiratorial mis-associations.

Examining image retrieval results for age-related and generational family-role terms (e.g., 'Aunty', 'Abuela', 'Mummy', 'school girl') to identify inappropriate sexualization and the presence of pornographic content.
Measuring the prevalence of NSFW and pornographic text flags in the metadata for images retrieved using religious search terms (e.g., 'Nun').
